privacy_intro: {operator} runs {site}, and answers for the personal data kept here. This page says what that is, and why.
privacy_collect_login: When you log in: your name, email address and an id from where you log in, to know who you are.
privacy_collect_signup: When you sign up for an event: your name and email address, and, as a guest, your phone number and company if you give them; your answers to the event's questions, if it asks; and the language you signed up in. What you can't eat, if the event asks and you tell us, is kept for the event without your name.
privacy_collect_editing: When you organize events: what you write, and who wrote what.
privacy_why: To hold events: organizers see who's coming and their answers, and a list of what people can't eat without names, to plan. We email you about the events you sign up for: that you're signed up, if the time changes, if it's cancelled, and a reminder the day before.
privacy_who: Those who log in see who has signed up for events, with their details. Everyone else sees only how many. Emails go out through our email provider, and pictures are kept with our storage provider.
privacy_keep: Your signup is deleted 30 days after the event has ended, with the event's list of what people can't eat. You can cancel it until sign-up closes, and organizers can take it off any time. What you can't eat stays with the event when you cancel, since nothing ties it to you.
privacy_cookies: When you log in, a cookie keeps you logged in. Your browser remembers the language and theme you pick and, if you signed up as a guest, the link to your signup.
privacy_cookies_hubspot: We use HubSpot for visitor statistics. HubSpot sets cookies to see how the site is used, and you choose which in the cookie settings.
privacy_rights: You can ask to see the data kept about you, and have it corrected or deleted.
